Theorem
[parallel tensors on irreducible manifolds]

Source: petersen:page-0399 ↗ thm:pet-ch10-de-rham-decomposition 1. ch10:10.3.2Let $(M,g)$ be an irreducible Riemannian manifold with a parallel $(1,1)$-tensor $T$. Then the symmetric part $S= frac 12(T+T^*)$ and skew-symmetric part $A= frac 12(T-T^*)$ each have exactly one (complex) eigenvalue. If $A e 0$, it induces (after scaling) a parallel complex structure, i.e. a Kähler structure.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch10-parallel-tensor-eigenvalue \sketch Metric compatibility implies

\[ g(( abla _XT)Y,Z)=g(Y,( abla _XT^*)Z), \]

so $T^*$, $S$, and $A$ are parallel. Every real eigenspace of $S$, and every real invariant subspace associated with a conjugate pair of eigenvalues of $A$, is therefore preserved by holonomy. Irreducibility leaves only one such summand in each decomposition. Thus $S$ is scalar and the nonzero skew-adjoint $A$ satisfies $A^2=-\mu ^2I$ for one $\mu >0$. Then $J=\mu ^{-1}A$ is parallel and $J^2=-I$, which is the required Kähler structure.

□
